parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain the origin of colour in transition element complexes.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Hexaaquanickel(II) ions are green. They form a green precipitate with hydroxide ions, $\text{OH}^{-}$, in equilibrium 1 and a blue complex with ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$, in equilibrium 2.

equilibrium 1 $\quad [\text{Ni}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+} + 2\text{OH}^{-} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ni}(\text{OH})_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$
 green ppt.

equilibrium 2 $\quad [\text{Ni}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+} + 6\text{NH}_3 \rightleftharpoons [\text{Ni}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{2+} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$
 blue
parts.text: Use Le Chatelier's principle to suggest explanations for the following observations.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Explain why when aqueous $\text{NH}_3$ is added dropwise to $[\text{Ni}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ a green precipitate is formed.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why when a large excess of aqueous $\text{NH}_3$ is added to $[\text{Ni}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$, the green precipitate dissolves and a blue solution is formed.
